2608.19710.title: Robust Cross-Modal Foundation Model Perception for Underwater Robots under Degraded Visual Conditions
2608.19710.paper_summary: Reliable underwater robotic perception remains difficult because optical imagery degrades under turbidity, wavelength-dependent attenuation, low illumination, scattering, and blur. Although sonar provides complementary information that is less affected by optical visibility, prior visual-sonar research has largely focused on feature alignment and nominal detection performance. We investigate cross-modal robustness as visual reliability deteriorates and assess whether pretrained visual foundation-model representations can be complemented by sonar under severe degradation. We use frozen DINOv2 as the visual encoder and construct a controlled five-level benchmark ranging from clean to extreme visual conditions. We compare conventional visual detection, frozen foundation-model representations, sonar context, fixed multimodal fusion, clean-trained adaptive gating, and degradation-aware gated fusion. Our method trains the fusion mechanism across the full range of degradation while keeping the visual and sonar encoders frozen, allowing modality contributions to adapt without fine-tuning the pretrained backbone. Under extreme combined degradation, the DINOv2 baseline achieves 0.4610 balanced accuracy, while degradation-aware visual-sonar fusion reaches 0.6152, a 33.5% relative improvement. The learned sonar contribution increases from 14.2% under clean conditions to 41.3% under extreme degradation, demonstrating adaptive redistribution of cross-modal reliance. Fusion provides the largest gains under severe turbidity and blur, whereas color attenuation alone yields little additional benefit. These results show that foundation-model representations remain valuable but insufficient under severe information loss, and that explicitly adapting fusion to modality reliability can improve robust underwater multimodal perception.
2608.19710.paper_summary_zh: 可靠的水下機器人感知仍然困難，因為光學影像在混濁、波長依賴的衰減、低光照、散射和模糊的情況下會退化。雖然聲納提供的補充信息不太受光學可見度的影響，但先前的視覺-聲納研究主要集中在特徵對齊和名義檢測性能上。我們研究了隨著視覺可靠性下降的跨模態穩健性，並評估在嚴重退化情況下，預訓練的視覺基礎模型表徵是否可以通過聲納來補充。我們使用凍結的 DINOv2 作為視覺編碼器，並構建了一個從清晰到極端視覺條件的五級控制基準。我們比較了傳統的視覺檢測、凍結的基礎模型表徵、聲納上下文、固定的多模態融合、清晰訓練的自適應閘控和退化感知的閘控融合。我們的方法在保持視覺和聲納編碼器凍結的同時，訓練融合機制跨越整個退化範圍，允許模態貢獻在不微調預訓練主幹的情況下進行適應。在極端的綜合退化下，DINOv2 基線達到 0.4610 的平衡準確率，而退化感知的視覺-聲納融合達到 0.6152，提升了 33.5% 的相對改善。學習到的聲納貢獻在清晰條件下從 14.2% 增加到極端退化下的 41.3%，顯示出跨模態依賴的自適應重分配。在嚴重的混濁和模糊下，融合提供了最大的增益，而僅僅是顏色衰減則幾乎沒有額外的好處。這些結果表明，基礎模型表徵在嚴重信息損失下仍然有價值，但不足以應對，並且明確地將融合適應於模態可靠性可以改善穩健的水下多模態感知。
2608.19710.author: Mohammad Arif Ul Alam et.al.
